I compiled the real endpoints and auth details from your code. Now I’ll deliver a concise, skimmable integration guide your frontend can use immediately.

### Base
- Local: `http://localhost:3000/api`
- Prod: `https://app.arzansite.com/api`
- Global prefix: `/api`

### Auth model
- Prefer cookie-based auth in browsers: backend sets HttpOnly cookie `appwrite_jwt` via `POST /api/auth/session` with `{ jwt }` from Appwrite `account.createJWT()`.
- Alternatively, send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` where token can be:
  - Backend JWT (from `auth/login`, `auth/refresh`, etc.)
  - Appwrite JWT (guard will validate with Appwrite)
- CORS: set `credentials: 'include'`. Origins must be allowed via `CORS_ORIGINS`.

### Required headers
- JSON: `Content-Type: application/json`
- Auth: send cookie automatically with `credentials: 'include'` OR header `Authorization: Bearer <token>`
- File uploads: `multipart/form-data`

### Response shape
- Success: `{ success: true, data: <payload>, timestamp: ISO }` (via TransformInterceptor) for most controllers. Some endpoints return raw shapes as coded.
- Error: `{ success: false, error: string, errorCode?: string, errorDetails?: string, timestamp: ISO }` (ErrorInterceptor) or standard Nest error `{ statusCode, message, error, ... }` from HttpExceptionFilter for some cases.

### Status codes and frontend handling
- 200 OK: parse JSON normally
- 201 Created: creation success
- 204 No Content: deletion success (no body)
- 400 Bad Request: validation/user input; show message, highlight fields if available
- 401 Unauthorized: refresh or re-auth; if using cookie, redirect to login/session creation
- 403 Forbidden: hide/disable UI, show “no permission”
- 404 Not Found: show friendly missing state
- 429 Too Many Requests: backoff/retry UI
- 500 Server Error: generic error, allow retry

### Auth endpoints `/auth`
- POST `/auth/signup`
  - Body: `{ email, password, metadata? }`
  - 201: user created + verification email
- POST `/auth/verify-email`
  - Body: `{ token, userId? }`
  - 200: email verified
- POST `/auth/password-reset`
  - Body: `{ email }`
  - 200: reset email sent
- POST `/auth/login`
  - Body: `{ email, password }`
  - 200: `{ access_token, refresh_token, user, session?, redirect? }`
- POST `/auth/refresh`
  - Body: `{ refresh_token }`
  - 200: `{ access_token, user }`
- POST `/auth/logout` (Bearer required)
  - 200: logout
- GET `/auth/me` (Bearer required)
  - 200: current user info
- POST `/auth/session`  [cookie-based]
  - Body: `{ jwt }` (Appwrite JWT)
  - 200: sets cookie `appwrite_jwt`, returns `{ user, message }`
- POST `/auth/userinfo` (Appwrite JWT via header/cookie)
  - 200: `{ user }`
- POST `/auth/exchange-jwt`
  - Body: `{ appwriteJwt }`
  - 200: backend JWT tokens `{ access_token, refresh_token, user }`
- POST `/auth/session-auth`
  - Body: `{ sessionId?, email?, password? }` (either sessionId+email or email+password)
  - 200: backend JWT tokens
- POST `/auth/session-logout`
  - Body: `{ sessionId }`
  - 200: session invalidated
- GET `/auth/session-info/:sessionId`
- POST `/auth/session-validate` Body: `{ sessionId }` → `{ valid, sessionId }`
- OAuth helpers:
  - POST `/auth/oauth/:provider/start` Body: `{ successUrl, failureUrl }` → `{ redirectUrl }`
  - POST `/auth/oauth/:provider/callback` Body: `{ userId, secret }` → sets cookies + redirect
  - GET `/auth/oauth/providers`
  - GET `/auth/oauth/me`
  - POST `/auth/oauth/logout` clears cookies

Frontend example (cookie flow):
```javascript
// Create Appwrite session, then JWT, then backend cookie
const { jwt } = await account.createJWT();
await fetch(`${API}/auth/session`, {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  credentials: 'include',
  body: JSON.stringify({ jwt })
});
// Call protected
const res = await fetch(`${API}/profiles/me`, { credentials: 'include' });
```

### Frontend patterns

- Fetch with cookie auth:
```javascript
const get = (path) => fetch(`${API}${path}`, { credentials: 'include' })
  .then(r => r.ok ? r.json() : r.json().then(e => Promise.reject(e)));

await get('/profiles/me');
```

- Fetch with bearer:
```javascript
const authFetch = (path, options={}) =>
  fetch(`${API}${path}`, {
    ...options,
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, ...(options.headers||{}) },
  }).then(r => r.ok ? r.json() : r.json().then(e => Promise.reject(e)));
```

- Error handling:
```javascript
try {
  const res = await get('/invoices');
} catch (e) {
  if (e.errorCode === 'UNAUTHORIZED' || e.statusCode === 401) { /* re-auth */ }
  else if (e.errorCode === 'FORBIDDEN' || e.statusCode === 403) { /* show no access */ }
  else { /* show e.error || e.message */ }
}
```

- File upload:
```javascript
const fd = new FormData();
fd.append('file', file);
fd.append('orderId', orderId);
await fetch(`${API}/uploads`, { method: 'POST', body: fd, credentials: 'include' });
```

- Payment request + verify:

const { paymentUrl, authority } = await authFetch('/payments/request', {
  method: 'POST',
  body: JSON.stringify({ amount, description, callbackUrl })
});
window.location.href = paymentUrl;
// After callback:
const verify = await authFetch('/payments/verify', {
  method: 'POST',
  body: JSON.stringify({ authority, amount })
});
```

- Wallet deposit:

  method: 'POST',
  body: JSON.stringify({ amount: 3000000, description: 'شارژ کیف پول' })
});
window.location.href = paymentUrl;
```

Notes
- Always use `credentials: 'include'` when using cookie-based auth.
- For admin endpoints, ensure token user has `role: admin` in Appwrite roles collection.
- For large bodies, server limit is 30MB. Use multipart for files.
- Swagger at `/api/docs` for live testing.

- If integration still fails, verify:
  - CORS_ORIGINS includes your frontend origin.
  - Cookies have correct domain/secure flags for prod.
  - Using HTTPS in production for `SameSite=None; Secure` cookies.

- Health check quickly:
```bash
curl http://localhost:3000/health
```

### Addendum: Implementation notes your frontend should follow (Appwrite + OAuth + Messaging)

#### Appwrite database ownership and shape (orders)
- Use `user_id` (snake_case) consistently in DB; never send it from the client.
  - Backend injects ownership from the authenticated context on create/update.
  - If you send `userId/userid`, the schema may reject with “Missing required attribute "userId"” or similar; the correct field is `user_id` and is server-managed.
- Expected permissions set by backend per document:
  - Read: `Role.user(user_id)`
  - Write: `Role.user(user_id)`
- Frontend implications:
  - Do not include `user_id` in payloads.
  - Expect 403/404 when accessing non-owned documents.
  - Prefer listing “mine” via query flag where available.

Create order (client, do NOT send user_id):
```json
{
  "title": "Website Design",
  "description": "Modern responsive website",
  "price": 15000000,
  "sessionId": "wizard_abc123"
}
```

Key endpoints you will use in this codebase:
- Create: `POST /api/orders`
- List mine: `GET /api/orders?mine=true` (default behavior for non-admins)
- Get one: `GET /api/orders/:id`
- Update: `PATCH /api/orders/:id`
- Delete: `DELETE /api/orders/:id`

#### Preferred Appwrite storage wrappers (low-level file ops)
Use these when you need raw Appwrite storage behaviors (otherwise use `/uploads` for business-level uploads):
- Upload: `POST /api/storage/upload/:bucketId` (multipart `file`)
- List: `GET /api/storage/:bucketId`
- Get URL: `GET /api/storage/:bucketId/:fileId/url`
- Delete: `DELETE /api/storage/:bucketId/:fileId`

Examples (cookie/session auth or Bearer):
```javascript
// Upload
const fd = new FormData();
fd.append('file', file);
await fetch(`${API}/storage/upload/${bucketId}`, {
  method: 'POST',
  body: fd,
  credentials: 'include'
});

// List
const files = await fetch(`${API}/storage/${bucketId}`, { credentials: 'include' }).then(r=>r.json());

// Direct view URL
const { url } = await fetch(`${API}/storage/${bucketId}/${fileId}/url`, { credentials: 'include' }).then(r=>r.json());

// Delete
await fetch(`${API}/storage/${bucketId}/${fileId}`, { method: 'DELETE', credentials: 'include' });
```

Notes:
- In production, ensure HTTPS so cookies with `SameSite=None; Secure` are sent.
- For user-facing attachments tied to orders, prefer the high-level `/api/uploads` endpoints.

#### OAuth choices (pick one)
- Appwrite-managed OAuth (recommended for browser apps):
  1) `account.createOAuth2Session(provider, successUrl, failureUrl)` via Appwrite JS SDK
  2) On success page, call backend: `POST /api/auth/session` with `account.createJWT()` result, or `POST /api/auth/exchange-jwt` to get backend JWT
  3) Call protected endpoints with `credentials: 'include'` (cookie) or `Authorization: Bearer <backend JWT>`

- Nest-managed OAuth:
  1) `POST /api/auth/oauth/:provider/start` with `{ successUrl, failureUrl }`
  2) Redirect user to `redirectUrl`
  3) Provider callback hits `POST /api/auth/oauth/:provider/callback`; backend sets cookies and finalizes
  4) Frontend continues with session cookie (no header needed)

Minimal code (Appwrite-managed):
```javascript
// after createOAuth2Session redirect:
const { jwt } = await account.createJWT();
await fetch(`${API}/auth/session`, {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  credentials: 'include',
  body: JSON.stringify({ jwt })
});
// now call protected:
await fetch(`${API}/profiles/me`, { credentials: 'include' });
```

#### Realtime/messaging role topics
- Valid subscribe roles: `any`, `guests`, `users`, `user:<USER_ID>`, `team:<ID>`, `member:<ID>`, `label:<ID>`
- Replace usage of `me` with `user:<USER_ID>` (you have user_id from `/auth/me` or `/profiles/me`)
- Example (Appwrite JS):
```javascript
client.subscribe([`user:${userId}`], (event) => {
  // handle changes
});
```

#### Authentication reminders
- Base URLs: local `http://localhost:3000/api`, prod `https://app.arzansite.com/api`
- Global prefix: `/api`
- Browser apps: prefer cookie session via `POST /auth/session` + `credentials: 'include'`
- Bearer option also works: `Authorization: Bearer <backend JWT>` or Appwrite JWT
- CORS: make sure your frontend origin is listed in `CORS_ORIGINS`. Always send `credentials: 'include'` when using cookies.

#### Status codes (what to do)
- 200/201: proceed
- 204: treat as success with no content
- 400: show validation messages; correct inputs
- 401: re-auth; if cookie-based, recreate session via `/auth/session`
- 403: hide/disable UI for unauthorized resources
- 404: show “not found”
- 429: backoff/retry
- 500: generic failure, allow retry

- Health check:
```bash
curl http://localhost:3000/health
```

- Correct auth endpoints for this backend:
  - Register: `POST /api/auth/signup` (not `/auth/register`)
  - Login: `POST /api/auth/login`
  - Current user: `GET /api/auth/me` (JWT) or `GET /api/profiles/me` (profile)
  - Session cookie: `POST /api/auth/session` with `{ jwt }`

- For orders and all DB-backed resources, client should never send `user_id`; backend sets it and enforces owner permissions.

- If you have legacy client code using `userId/userid`, update payloads to remove ownership fields and let the server assign `user_id`.

- For files tied to orders, the recommended user path is:
  - Upload: `POST /api/uploads` (multipart `file`, optional `orderId`, `fileType`)
  - List: `GET /api/uploads?orderId=...`
  - Get: `GET /api/uploads/:id?bucketType=...`
  - Delete: `DELETE /api/uploads/:id?bucketType=...`

- For raw Appwrite storage use cases, prefer the `/api/storage/*` wrappers listed above.

- Messaging: always subscribe using explicit roles, e.g. `user:<user_id>`.

- Handle 401 by re-establishing session cookie or refreshing tokens before retrying protected calls.

- Ensure HTTPS in production to transmit cookies (`SameSite=None; Secure`).

- Summary

Short answer: No. You do not need (and should not) use Appwrite in the frontend. Use only your backend endpoints. The earlier notes included an optional Appwrite-managed OAuth flow, but here’s the backend-only approach your frontend should follow.

### What to avoid in the frontend
- Do not import or call Appwrite SDK.
- Do not call `account.createJWT()` or `account.createOAuth2Session()`.

### Backend-only auth flows (pick one)

- Email/password (pure backend)
  - Register: POST `/api/auth/signup` with `{ email, password, metadata? }`
  - Login: POST `/api/auth/login` → `{ access_token, refresh_token, user }`
  - Use: Send `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` for all protected endpoints
  - Refresh: POST `/api/auth/refresh` with `{ refresh_token }`

- OAuth (backend-managed)
  - Start: POST `/api/auth/oauth/:provider/start` with `{ successUrl, failureUrl }` → `redirectUrl`
  - Redirect user to `redirectUrl`
  - Callback: backend handles `/api/auth/oauth/:provider/callback`, sets cookies/tokens
  - Use: Call protected endpoints with `credentials: 'include'` (no Appwrite SDK)

Example (email/password):
```javascript
// login
const login = await fetch(`${API}/auth/login`, {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ email, password })
}).then(r => r.json());

// call protected endpoints
const res = await fetch(`${API}/profiles/me`, {
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${login.access_token}` }
});
```

### Orders and DB data
- Do not send ownership fields like `user_id`. The backend injects `user_id` and sets Appwrite permissions.
- If legacy payloads have `userId/userid`, remove them on the client.

### Files
- Use backend only:
  - Higher-level: `/api/uploads` (recommended for user/order files)
  - Low-level Appwrite wrappers: `/api/storage/*` (no Appwrite SDK needed)
```javascript
const fd = new FormData();
fd.append('file', file);
await fetch(`${API}/uploads`, { method: 'POST', body: fd, credentials: 'include' });
```

### Realtime (optional)
- If you need realtime without Appwrite in the frontend, proxy via your backend (WebSocket/SSE). Avoid subscribing directly to Appwrite channels in the frontend.

### Checklist to ensure no Appwrite in the frontend
- No `appwrite` dependency in the frontend
- All auth via `/auth/*` (login/refresh or backend-managed OAuth)
- All data via backend routes (orders, wallets, invoices, uploads)
- No direct calls to Appwrite endpoints; no Appwrite tokens handled by the frontend

If you’d like, I can strip Appwrite-front references from your docs and produce a Postman collection using only backend routes.

Here’s why those 500s are happening and how to fix them quickly.

### Why POST /api/orders returns 500
- Root cause: Schema mismatch in Appwrite “orders” collection vs what `OrdersService.createOrder()` writes.
  - Service writes fields like `user_id`, `title`, `description`, `price`, `status`, `comments`, `total_pages`, `total_sections`, `wizardData`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, etc.
  - Your existing collection likely has old fields like `userId`, `orderNumber`, `totalAmount`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, or is missing the new ones entirely.
  - Appwrite rejects unknown/missing attributes; the error gets wrapped and you see “Http Exception” 500.

What to do (server-side)
1) Align collection attributes with the service
- Ensure the “orders” collection has at least:
  - Strings: `user_id` (req), `title` (<=255), `description` (<=4000), `payment_status` (default 'pending'), `comments` (<=1000), `wizardData` (>=16384), `payment_gateway` (<=50), `callback_url` (<=500), `return_url` (<=500)
  - Numbers: `price` (float), `total_pages` (int), `total_sections` (int)
  - Datetime: `created_at`, `updated_at`
  - Strings: `status` (e.g., 'pending'|'in_progress'|'completed'|'cancelled')
- If you previously used `userId`, add `user_id` and keep `userId` only until you backfill and fully migrate.

2) Make create idempotent/secure and set owner permissions
- In `OrdersService.createOrder(...)`, pass document permissions:
```ts
import { Permission, Role } from 'node-appwrite';

// ...
await databases.createDocument(
  databaseId,
  ordersCollection,
  ID.unique(),
  { ...data }, // the same payload you have now
  [Permission.read(Role.user(userId)), Permission.write(Role.user(userId))]
);
```

3) Improve error visibility temporarily (so 500s show real cause)
- Wrap `createDocument` in try/catch and log `error.message` (and `error.response` if present) before re-throwing an HttpException.

4) Run your schema update
- If you need a quick stopgap for `wizardData` and `payment_status` run: `node update-orders-schema-simple.js`
- Then add the missing attributes listed in step 1 (either extend `update-orders-schema.js` or create a small add-attributes script) and deploy.

No frontend change needed for /orders payload. Keep sending what you’re sending; the backend owns `user_id`.

### Why POST /api/messaging/topics returns 500
- Root cause: You repeatedly create the same topic ID (deterministic from name), Appwrite returns 409 “already exists”, and the controller throws a generic Error → 500.
- Also ensure “subscribe” values are valid roles like `user:<USER_ID>` (yours look correct).

What to do (server-side)
- Make topic creation idempotent and return 200/201:
```ts
async createTopic(topicId: string, name: string, subscribe: string[]) {
  try {
    return await this.messaging.createTopic(topicId, name, subscribe);
  } catch (err: any) {
    if (err?.code === 409) {
      // treat as success; optionally fetch and return the topic if API supports it
      return { $id: topicId, name, subscribe };
    }
    throw new Error(`Failed to create topic: ${err.message}`);
  }
}
```
- Or in the controller, catch 409 and return a success response instead of throwing.

Frontend workaround (optional)
- If the topic is per-user, call the endpoint once on first login and ignore “already exists” responses, or gate on a local flag.

- Create order:

### Recommendation
- Use a simple roles collection in Appwrite Database (what you already have with `user_roles`). It’s lighter and already integrated with your backend’s `RolesGuard`. Teams are great for collaboration structures, but they’d require refactoring your guard to query team memberships. Labels aren’t for RBAC.
- Keep Appwrite document permissions for ownership (e.g., `Permission.read(Role.user(user_id))`). Use your DB role for application-level RBAC (user/admin).

### What to implement
- Collection: `user_roles` with fields:
  - `user_id: string` (unique index)
  - `role: 'user' | 'admin'`
- Default role on signup:
  - After user creation, insert `{ user_id: <id>, role: 'user' }` if not present.
- Expose role to frontend for protected pages:
  - Add role to auth responses (best DX) and/or a role endpoint.
  - Minimal change: enrich `GET /auth/me` to include `role`.
  - Optionally include `role` in login/refresh payloads so the frontend can gate UI immediately (do NOT trust it for enforcement; backend still enforces via `RolesGuard`).

### Minimal code edits (where)
- In `AuthService.signUp` (after profile creation): upsert default role.
- In `AuthService.getMe`: fetch `role` and return it.
- Optionally in `AuthService.signIn`, `loginWithJwt`, `refreshToken`, `authenticateWithSession`: include `role` in the returned `user` object (and optionally as a JWT claim for convenience).

Example for `getMe` (conceptual):
```ts
// inside AuthService.getMe(userId)
const databases = this.appwriteService.getDatabases();
const db = this.configService.get<string>('APPWRITE_DATABASE_ID');
const col = this.configService.get<string>('APPWRITE_COLLECTION_USER_ROLES');
const { Query } = await import('node-appwrite');
const docs = await databases.listDocuments(db, col, [Query.equal('user_id', userId), Query.limit(1)]);
const role = docs.documents?.[0]?.role ?? 'user';
return { id: userId, role };
```

Default role on signup:
```ts
// inside AuthService.signUp after profile creation
const db = this.configService.get('APPWRITE_DATABASE_ID');
const col = this.configService.get('APPWRITE_COLLECTION_USER_ROLES');
const { Query, ID } = await import('node-appwrite');
const exists = await this.appwriteService.getDatabases().listDocuments(db, col, [Query.equal('user_id', created.$id), Query.limit(1)]);
if (!exists.documents.length) {
  await this.appwriteService.getDatabases().createDocument(db, col, ID.unique(), { user_id: created.$id, role: 'user' });
}
```

Frontend usage
- After login or on app start, call `/api/auth/me` and read `{ role }` to gate routes (e.g., `role === 'admin'` for admin pages).
- Keep backend as the source of truth; rely on `RolesGuard` for actual protection.

Why not Teams/Labels?
- Teams: viable but heavier; you’d need to rework `RolesGuard` to check team membership and keep your admin team synced. Not necessary for simple user/admin RBAC.
- Labels: not designed for global RBAC; better for messaging/segmentation.

Summary
- Stick with `user_roles` collection (DB-based RBAC).
- Auto-create `role='user'` on signup.
- Return `role` from `/auth/me` (and optionally from login/refresh) so the frontend can show/hide protected pages.
- Keep enforcement server-side with your existing `RolesGuard`.

- I reviewed your upload stack. The existing routes under `uploads` already implement a proper server-side upload to Appwrite Storage and create a DB record in `project_files` via `UploadsService.uploadFile(...)`. But your frontend calls are hitting `POST /api/storage/upload/:bucketId`, whose controller previously returned a placeholder. I implemented real upload logic in `POST /storage/upload/:bucketId` so both paths now work.

What I changed
- `src/appwrite/storage.controller.ts`:
  - Implemented actual upload using a temp file stream and `storage.createFile(bucketId, fileId, stream, permissions)`.
  - Creates a metadata record in `project_files` after upload with both snake_case and camelCase fields:
    - file_id/fileId, user_id/userId, order_id/orderId, bucket_id/bucketId, original_name/originalName, mime_type/mimeType, size, created_at/createdAt, updated_at/updatedAt.
  - Sets per-file permissions:
    - read/write for the uploader: read("user:<userId>"), write("user:<userId>")
    - optional admin team access via APPWRITE_ADMIN_TEAM_ID: read("team:<id>"), write("team:<id>")

How to use it from the frontend
- Single file:
```http
POST /api/storage/upload/uploads
Content-Type: multipart/form-data
Authorization: Bearer <token>

file: <binary>
orderId: <optional-order-id>
```
- Response:
```json
{ "success": true, "fileId": "<id>", "name": "filename.ext", "bucketId": "uploads", "userId": "<uid>", "orderId": "<oid>", "permissions": ["read(\"user:<uid>\")", ...] }
```
- List my files later:
```http
GET /api/uploads?userId=<me optional>&orderId=<orderId optional>
```
- Or by id:
```http
GET /api/uploads/:id?bucketType=uploads
```

Recommendations and checks
- Buckets: In env, ensure the bucket keys you use (e.g., uploads, images, designs) exist and are mapped in `AppwriteConfig.buckets`.
- Collection: Create `project_files` with attributes (snake_case recommended): file_id, user_id, order_id, bucket_id, original_name, mime_type, size, created_at, updated_at. Make only file_id required; others optional.
- Permissions in collection: either disable document security or allow the server key to write. The record creation uses the same permissions list as the file so admins and the owner can read/write the record too.
- Optional admin access: set `APPWRITE_ADMIN_TEAM_ID` so admins can access all files.

Sample NestJS service/controller snippet (if you want to upload via uploads routes)
- Controller: already implemented in `src/uploads/uploads.controller.ts` (POST /api/uploads and POST /api/uploads/bulk).
- Service: `UploadsService.uploadFile(...)` writes to storage and to `project_files`.

Troubleshooting
- Files created but not visible: verify you’re uploading to the intended bucket key (e.g., uploads) and that this bucket exists in Appwrite. Check Appwrite console: Storage → the bucket you passed in the URL.
- DB record missing: ensure env `APPWRITE_COLLECTION_PROJECT_FILES` is set to the collection id/name; if you use a strict schema, confirm all required attributes exist and match names. The code writes both snake_case and camelCase to satisfy legacy schemas.

Next steps for you
- Try your existing frontend again:
  - It already calls `POST /api/storage/upload/uploads`. You should now see files in Appwrite Storage and a record in `project_files`.
- If you also use `/api/uploads` bulk flow, that’s already working and persists records as well.

If you want, I can also:
- Add a GET /api/storage/:bucketId/:fileId/url short-link responder into UI flow.
- Add a GET /api/storage/:bucketId search by user/order using `project_files` to avoid listing all files in buckets.
